keyVerseText: By these were the isles of the Gentiles divided in their lands; every one after his tongue, after their families, in their nations.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun גּוֹי (gôwy) derives from a root related to גֵּוָה (gêvâh), meaning 'body' or 'mass,' suggesting a concept of a gathered or assembled group. This etymology enriches the common English gloss of 'nation' or 'people' by emphasizing the collective nature of a people as a unified body or entity. Thus, גּוֹי carries the idea of a distinct community or massing of individuals, whether human or figurative, such as animals.
usageInScripture: The word גּוֹי is used extensively throughout the Hebrew Bible, appearing 561 times and primarily translated as 'nations' or 'Gentiles.' It consistently denotes groups of people, often non-Hebrew nations, but can also refer to the people of Israel or descendants of Abraham, highlighting its flexibility. The frequent translations such as 'among the heathen' or 'of the nations' reveal its role in distinguishing ethnic or national identities within the biblical narrative.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding גּוֹי as a term for a nation or people underscores the biblical emphasis on God's dealings not only with Israel but with all peoples. It reveals God's sovereign orchestration of diverse nations and peoples, each with distinct identities yet under His providential care. This term also points to the inclusivity of God's redemptive plan, which encompasses Gentiles alongside Israel, foreshadowing the gospel's extension to all nations through Christ. Recognizing the collective nature implied by גּוֹי invites believers to see the church as a new people formed from every nation.
keyVerseReflection: Genesis 10:5 states, 'By these were the isles of the Gentiles divided in their lands; every one after his tongue, after their families, in their nations.' Here, גּוֹי emphasizes the distinct and organized communities formed after the flood, each with its own language and territory. The use of גּוֹי highlights God's sovereign distribution and differentiation of peoples, setting the stage for the unfolding history of nations in Scripture.
